items.title: Pay claimed import duties to release parcel
items.computation: The letter states a fixed calendar date for payment: 09.11.2026. This is a demand from a private company, not a German authority, so no statutory deemed-delivery rule applies — the printed date stands as written. 09.11.2026 falls on a Monday, no weekend/holiday shift needed. Verified with the deadline tool (fixed date, nature=payment): due_date 2026-11-09.

warnings: This letter shows strong hallmarks of a parcel/customs phishing scam: the payee, 'Intl. Parcel Clearing Ltd.', has no relation to German customs — real German import VAT (Einfuhrumsatzsteuer) is collected only by the Zoll (Hauptzollamt), never by a private 'Paketzentrum' company via bank transfer.
The given IBAN (DE96 7001 0080 0661 2345 67) fails its own checksum validation and is very likely fake or mistyped — do not send money to it, and ideally do not pay at all.
Contact is restricted to a WhatsApp mobile number only, and the email domain 'clearance-mail.example' is not a genuine corporate or governmental domain — both are typical scam/phishing indicators.
The letter uses classic pressure tactics: a very short deadline (4 days from the letter's date) plus a threat to destroy or return the goods if payment is not received in time.

The recipient's postal code (37073, in the Göttingen/Niedersachsen area) does not match the Nordrhein-Westfalen region stated for this person — worth double-checking that this letter is even addressed to the right person.

Recommendation: do not pay or reply via the WhatsApp number or email given; instead verify any real parcel/customs charge directly through the shipping carrier's official tracking page or the Zoll's official channels.
